c.tagline: Singapore's northern gateway town - the Causeway to Malaysia, malls, and waterfront parks.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis (ComfortDelGro and others) are reliable; ride-hailing via Grab, Gojek, or TADA is equally common and priced up-front. Cross-border taxis run from Woodlands to Johor Bahru.

emergency.note: 999 reaches the police; 995 is for fire and ambulance emergencies.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The town's civic and commercial core around Woodlands Square, the large Causeway Point mall, Woods Square, the regional library, and the MRT and bus interchange; the most convenient and walkable base.
An older residential estate west of the center with Marsiling Park, Marsiling Mall, and its own MRT station, sitting right beside the Woodlands Checkpoint and the Causeway to Malaysia.
A quiet eastern residential neighborhood known for the award-winning Kampung Admiralty integrated village, 888 Plaza, and the mangrove-filled Admiralty Park; calm and family-friendly.
The smallest and greenest estate, home to most of Woodlands' private condominiums and landed houses, tucked between Marsiling and the waterfront; a relaxed, upscale residential pocket.

The northern coastal edge along Woodlands Waterfront Park and the Johor Strait, with jetty views of Malaysia, park connectors, Republic Polytechnic, and the future RTS Link terminus at Woodlands North.
lodging: Holiday Inn Express Singapore Clarke Quay

water.note: Singapore tap water is safe and rigorously tested.

transit.hours: MRT trains and buses run roughly 5:30 AM to midnight daily; after midnight, taxis, ride-hailing, and limited night buses fill the gap. The Johor Bahru-Singapore shuttle train and Causeway buses run cross-border on their own schedules.
transit.note: Woodlands is served by five MRT stations across two lines - the North-South Line (Marsiling, Woodlands, Admiralty) and the Thomson-East Coast Line (Woodlands North, Woodlands, Woodlands South) - plus an extensive bus network centred on the underground Woodlands Regional Bus Interchange. Woodlands North is the future terminus of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS Link).
transit.pay: Tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard or phone at MRT gates and on buses (SimplyGo), or use a stored-value EZ-Link/SimplyGo card sold at station offices and convenience stores. Fares are distance-based and inexpensive.

bus: Causeway Link and public buses to Johor Bahru (Malaysia)
train: Woodlands Train Checkpoint shuttle to Johor Bahru Sentral (Malaysia)

transit.m: MRT to Woodlands via the Thomson-East Coast / North-South lines (60-75 min, one change)
Airport shuttle to the city, then MRT north to Woodlands

tip.r: Not expected; a 10% service charge is usually already included on restaurant bills.

food.name: Bak chor mee
food.desc: Minced pork noodles tossed in vinegar, chilli and pork lard, topped with liver, meatballs and crisp fried sole - a northern breakfast staple.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Bright rooftop-village hawker centre above Admiralty MRT; several long-queue noodle stalls open from breakfast.

places.name: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre
places.note: Neighbourhood centre beside Marsiling MRT with cheap, consistently busy noodle and porridge stalls.

places.name: 888 Plaza Food Centre
places.note: Old-school HDB food centre that locals rate for classic wet and dry minced pork noodles.

food.name: Hokkien prawn mee
food.desc: Yellow noodles and rice vermicelli braised in a deep prawn-and-pork stock with squid, prawns and a knob of sambal and calamansi.

places.name: You Fu Claypot Delights
places.note: Woodlands favourite known for its hokkien prawn mee and sesame oil chicken; short walk from Admiralty MRT.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Fried noodle stalls here work over charcoal-style heat and draw steady weekend queues.

places.name: Woodlands Hawker Centre
places.note: Newer air-well hawker centre next to Woodlands MRT with a strong fried-noodle row.

food.name: Laksa
food.desc: Thick rice noodles cut short for the spoon, in a coconut-rich prawn and dried-shrimp gravy with cockles, fishcake and laksa leaf.

places.name: Ye Lai Xiang Laksa
places.note: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre stall regularly named among the north's best bowls of laksa.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Several Peranakan-style stalls; easy to pair a bowl with kueh from the wet market downstairs.

places.name: Causeway Point food hall
places.note: Air-conditioned option right at Woodlands MRT if the hawker centres are packed.

food.name: Teochew seafood soup
food.desc: Clear peppery broth simmered with fish bones, milk-white and studded with sliced fish, prawns, tofu and salted vegetable.

places.name: Yan Ji Seafood Soup
places.note: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre stall known for a proper Teochew-style broth and generous seafood.

places.name: Woodlands Hawker Centre
places.note: Reliable soup and porridge stalls; a good light meal after a day at the Causeway.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Fish soup stalls here open late morning through dinner, popular with the seniors living upstairs.

food.name: Nasi lemak and roti prata
food.desc: Coconut rice with sambal, ikan bilis and fried egg, or flaky griddled prata pulled to order and dunked in fish curry.

places.name: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre
places.note: Malay and Indian-Muslim stalls run early and late, handy for a pre-Causeway breakfast.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Halal stalls sit alongside the wet market; prata and murtabak are made to order.

places.name: 888 Plaza Food Centre
places.note: Long-running prata and nasi lemak counters that open before dawn for shift workers.

food.name: Middle Eastern hawker plates
food.desc: An unusual Woodlands twist - shawarma, mandi rice and grilled meats cooked hawker-style, a legacy of Singapore's Arab Street traders.

places.name: Taibah Arabic
places.note: Kampung Admiralty stall run by former Arab Street traders; named among 2025's best hawker finds.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: The centre deliberately mixes regional cuisines, so you can share plates across stalls.

places.name: Woodlands Hawker Centre
places.note: Halal-certified stalls and a mix of Thai, Indonesian and Malay cooking under one roof.

food.name: Kopi
food.desc: Robusta beans roasted with sugar and margarine, sock-filtered and served with condensed milk - order kopi-o kosong for it black and unsweetened.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Traditional drinks stalls pull kopi from dawn; the rooftop garden is a fine place to drink it.

places.name: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre
places.note: Classic sock-filter coffee stalls that still serve in thick ceramic cups if you sit in.

places.name: 888 Plaza Food Centre
places.note: Old-school kopitiam drinks counter, cheap and unfussy, popular with morning regulars.

food.name: Teh tarik and sugarcane juice
food.desc: Condensed-milk tea pulled between two mugs until frothy, or ice-cold pressed sugarcane with lemon - the standard Causeway-heat antidotes.

places.name: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre
places.note: Indian-Muslim drinks stalls do proper high-pull teh tarik alongside fresh juices.

places.name: Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre
places.note: Fresh fruit and sugarcane stalls press to order; a cheap refill point before crossing to Johor.

places.name: Woodlands Hawker Centre
places.note: Juice stalls beside the MRT exit, convenient for travellers heading to the Causeway.

landmarks: The Woodlands Waterway
A scenic 1.25-mile man-made canal lined with public art, fountains, and water taxis that serves as the town's signature promenade.
Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion
This open-air amphitheater is the region's premier concert venue and an architectural centerpiece framed by lush greenery.
Waterway Square
A grand public plaza with a dramatic fountain show and sweeping staircases overlooking the Waterway, popular for photos day and night.
Market Street, The Woodlands
An upscale open-air shopping and dining district with charming streetscapes, seasonal decor, and a lively town-center atmosphere.
Riva Row Boat House
A picturesque boathouse on the Waterway offering kayak and paddleboat rentals against a postcard-worthy waterfront backdrop.
Hughes Landing Waterfront
A vibrant lakefront development on Lake Woodlands with skyline views, restaurants, and a lively promenade popular at sunset.
Lake Woodlands
The community's central lake offers tranquil water views, sailing, and one of the best sunset photo spots in the area.
Town Green Park
A leafy central park with an ice rink in winter and a green lawn for concerts, anchoring the heart of Town Center.
Northshore Park
A lakeside park with walking trails, a pavilion, and skyline views across Lake Woodlands, ideal for peaceful nature photography.
The Woodlands Mall
One of the area's architectural and shopping landmarks, notable as a longtime community gathering hub and retail icon.

intl.to: Johor Bahru (Malaysia) - ~5 min from Woodlands Train Checkpoint

train.note: Woodlands is where Singapore's only international train leaves from: the KTMB Shuttle Tebrau crosses the Causeway to JB Sentral in about five minutes, with immigration for both countries cleared before boarding. Tickets go on sale 30 days ahead and sell out within minutes at peak times, so book the moment the window opens. Singapore has no domestic long-distance rail - the MRT North-South line serves Woodlands locally.

intl.op: SBS Transit service 170 / SMRT 950 — tickets on board

bus.note: The Causeway buses from Woodlands are the cheap alternative to the train, but you get off twice for immigration at Woodlands and Johor checkpoints and queues can be very long at weekends and holidays. The 950 and Causeway Link services run every few minutes through the day. Bring your passport and small change or a stored-value card.

ferry.note: There is no ferry from Woodlands - it faces the narrow Johor Strait, crossed by the Causeway. Singapore's international sailings to the Indonesian islands leave from HarbourFront and Tanah Merah terminals on the south and east coasts.

half.name: Johor Bahru
half.blurb: Johor Bahru is a Malaysian city across the Causeway from Woodlands, with malls, markets and the Sultan Abu Bakar Mosque.

half.name: Legoland Malaysia
half.blurb: Legoland Malaysia is a theme park in Johor with Lego-themed rides and an adjoining water park.

full.name: Desaru Coast
full.blurb: Desaru Coast is a beach resort area on Malaysia's east coast with sandy shoreline and golf courses.
